record.context_brief: Arithmetic progressions in sets with diverging reciprocals
record.original_question: Suppose that A N has the property that the sum of the reciprocal of the elements of A diverges: P a2A 1=a = 1. Must A contain k-term arithmetic progressions for all k 3? Even the case k = 3 is open.

evidence.quote: Arithmetic progressions in sets with diverging reciprocals. (Erd}os-Tur an) Suppose that A N has the property that the sum of the reciprocal of the elements of A diverges: P a2A 1=a = 1. Must A contain k-term arithmetic progressions for all k 3? Even the case k = 3 is open.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be a set of positive integers such that $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a} = \infty$. Must $A$ contain a $k$-term arithmetic progression (that is, a set of the form $\{x, x+d, x+2d, \ldots, x+(k-1)d\}$ with $d \geq 1$) for every integer $k \geq 3$? Resolve in particular the case $k = 3$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is the well-known Erdős conjecture on arithmetic progressions. It remains open in general. Bloom and Sisask (2020) proved that any subset of {1,...,N} with no 3-term AP has size O(N/(log N)^{1+c}) for some c>0, which is the first bound past the "logarithmic barrier" but still does not resolve even the k=3 case of the conjecture for all sets with divergent reciprocal sum (it would, however, if improved to bounds quantitatively sufficient — and indeed their bound does imply the k=3 case). Subsequent refinements (Kelley–Meka 2023) gave much stronger 3-AP bounds, which imply the k=3 case of Erdős's conjecture. For k ≥ 4 the conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Erdős conjecture on arithmetic progressions
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture remains open for k ≥ 4; the case k=3 follows from results on 3-term progression bounds.
status_evidence.claim: The general conjecture for all k≥3 is still open.
